evidence: STATIC STRUCTURE (no inversion found). (1) Policy is template-identical: sha256 of task tests/scoring.toml (95f70d6e...), tools/score.py (13de2b38...), test.sh (bd682592...), restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile all equal the frozen template copies. scoring.toml: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4); the skill's example inversion 'craft carrying more mass than function' does not occur. (2) score.py lines 40-48: reward = weighted mean only if every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, else 0.0. I copied score.py+scoring.toml to my scratchpad (not the workspace) and ran it with python -B on synthetic reward.json files: F/P/V 0.05/1/1 -> 0.0; 0.0513/1/1 -> 0.4308; 1/1/1 -> 1.0; render gate 0 with perfect scored -> 0.0 (exit 1). A Pareto sweep over 117 (F,P,V) points (F in 0..1 step 0.1 plus 0.05/0.0501, P,V in {0,0.5,1}) found 0 dominance violations of 13689 ordered pairs: no app that is at least as good on every dimension ever scores lower. (3) Per-dimension aggregation is weighted_mean with positive weights (functional 43 criteria, sum 58.5, min 0.5; polish 5 binary, sum 12; visual 5 likert points=5 weight 1.2 each), so passing an extra criterion can only raise a dimension. (4) Gates cannot be failed by a stronger conforming app: render gate (wrong password stays signed out, Rafael signs in to a usable workspace) and constraints gate (Recruiter opens job with title/team/hiring manager/2 places, adds candidate with name/email/source; Observer in an independent context sees the job and exactly one Applied card) only ask what hireops_rules.md §1-§3 require (job fields §2, card starts at bottom of Applied §2, Observer reads the board §1). (5) Dead-app farming is blocked: every scored prompt repeats the browser gate that zeros a static shell; refusal rows carry explicit positive controls (e.g. hro_mgr_early_refused 'their late-stage moves are the control', hro_observer_readonly 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control', hro_anonymous 'A signed-in success of each is the control', hro_undo_full 'the other successful undos ... are the control', hro_pol_live_board 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'); polish rows grade concurrency preservation and require a live update, so a non-live app cannot farm polish. With gate-guaranteed job_open+add_candidate worth only 1.0/58.5=0.017 functional (< 0.05 floor), a gate-only pretty app still gets reward 0. (6) Weights track brief emphasis: the brief's 'hard part' items carry the largest functional weights (hro_stale_refused 2.5, hro_live_board 2.5, hro_candidate_private 2.5, undo/bulk 1.5-2) versus intake 0.5. ACCEPTED NON-STRICT CASES (not inversions, recorded for the owner): (a) Cross-dimension trade inherent to the mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 profile: functional 0.0513 + polish 0.29 + visual 1.0 -> 0.2888 beats functional 0.35 + polish 0 + visual 0.25 -> 0.26 (measured with frozen score.py). The apps are not Pareto-ordered, the weights are the skill-mandated profile and template-controlled, so this is not a task defect. (b) Vacuous-pass rows: hro_activity (weight 1) and hro_activity_refusals (0.5) can be easier for an app with fewer successful/refused actions, but the same app loses far more weight on the move/refusal rows, so total order is not inverted. RUNTIME (unmeasured, hence risk). raw-evidence-index.json (sha256 66854be5...; entry hashes 749036d0..., 1c7e6fcc..., 6752f461... re-verified; frozen solution server.js 4fc5d2c4..., src/index.js b07109f8..., board.js a177dc0c... match) states: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' REVIEW_POLICY requires hash-bound runtime records for reward discrimination and reward ordering before clearance; none exists. The specific unmeasured inversion path: the functional judge runs 14 long protocols (S..D, many independent contexts, replays and 15-second live waits) under judge timeout 9000 inside `timeout 11100 rewardkit ...` (test.sh:207, :224-226); if the scored suite fails or times out, test.sh exits leaving the zero reward written at the start, and each prompt maps an exhausted budget to binary 0 / Likert 1 ('NOT EXERCISED — evaluator/tool limitation'). Whether a fully working app (more successful steps, more readbacks) or a broken one (repeated re-setup on new jobs per functional prompt line 13) is more likely to exhaust the budget is unknown without a configured judge run, so budget-driven rank inversion cannot be excluded. No Docker, judge, Oracle, model or portal run was performed by this reviewer.
